podcast.title: Rise in 1993
podcast.body: The Tea Party began their rise in 1993, joining a wave of new Canadian artists gaining attention both domestically and internationally. This marked a period when foreign music fans started discovering Canadian talent. "1993, Doe Boys, the Tea Party, Daniel Landwaw, More Sarah McLaughlin, More Pursuit of Happiness, More Cowboy Junkeys."

podcast.title: Breakup Due to Creative Differences
podcast.body: The band broke up around 2005 due to "creative differences," leading to a period where individual members pursued separate projects. This internal conflict temporarily ended their collaborative work. "the whole creative differences things settled in and the band broke up."

podcast.body: Drummer Jeff Burrows joined the band Crash Karma, which featured ex-members from R.L.I.D.P., Somanova, and Edwin. He also dedicates his time to various charitable causes. podcast.title: Jeff Martin's Solo Career and Production Work
podcast.body: After The Tea Party's initial breakup, Jeff Martin moved to Ireland to launch a solo career. He subsequently formed the bands The Armada and Jeff Martin 777, and also worked as a producer for various artists. "Jeff moved to Ireland to start a solo career then came a band called the Armada followed by Jeff Martin 777 and he also served as a producer for a number of acts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Long Album Run and International Sales
podcast.body: The group maintained a 15-year album run from 1990 to 2005, achieving "hundreds of thousands of records" in sales both in Canada and internationally, notably in Australia. This showcases their significant commercial success and global appeal. "The group had a 15 year album run from 1990 to 2005 selling hundreds of thousands of records at home and places like yes Australia."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the '90s: Part 1

podcast.title: Origin and Location
podcast.body: The Tea Party originated from Windsor, Ontario, with all three band members hailing from the city. Jeff Martin's later residence in Perth, Australia, highlights the global reach of their careers. "Perth is on the west coast of Australia and this is where you'll find Jeff Martin of the Tea Party which is a long way from Windsor Ontario which is where all three members of the band are from."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Can Rock Revolution Survival
podcast.body: The Tea Party's career continued successfully long after the 1990s, indicating the enduring impact of the Can Rock Revolution. "Many acts survived long after the decade ended. The tragically hip, Sloan, R80p, Serma Glockland, Tea Party, Matt Good, many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 90s Part 8: The CanRock Revolution

podcast.title: Reunion and Continued Activity
podcast.body: The Tea Party reunited in 2011, a reunion that has proven successful and enduring. Since then, the band has toured, released new music including *The Ocean at the End of the World* in 2014, and issued anniversary sets. "Now in 2011 there was a full on Tea Party reunion which has stuck by the way the band is toured released an album called The Ocean at the end of the world which was in 2014 and issued an anniversary set or two."

podcast.title: Stuart Chatwood's Misophonia Project
podcast.body: Stuart Chatwood is actively involved in a project called Uncommon Folk, which aims to support individuals diagnosed with misophonia. This sensory processing disorder causes negative emotional and physical reactions to specific sounds. "Stuart is also working on a project called Uncommon Folk which seeks to help people diagnosed with a sensory processing disorder called mesophonia."

podcast.title: Stuart Chatwood's Video Game Soundtrack Work
podcast.body: Bassist and keyboardist Stuart Chatwood became a prominent producer of music for video games, composing soundtracks for eight *Prince of Persia* games for Ubisoft, which collectively sold 10 million copies, as well as the soundtrack for *Darkest Dungeon*. This showcases his significant contributions to the gaming industry. "Basin keyboard player Stuart Chatwood is a producer of music for video games he did the soundtracks for eight prince of Persia games for Ubisoft which collectively have sold 10 million copies and he did the soundtrack for another game called Darkest Dungeon."

xref.title: Stuart Chatwood as Bass Player Candidate
xref.body: Stuart Chatwood, the bassist and keyboardist for The Tea Party, was considered a strong candidate for the bass player position in The Smashing Pumpkins, although the opportunity ultimately did not materialize. This reflects his high esteem within the music industry. "for a while he was a strong candidate to be the bass player for the smashing pumpkins but that ended up not working out."

xref.title: Vocal Style Development
xref.body: Ben, the vocalist, initially spent the first five years of the band trying to emulate other singers like Eddie Vedder, Scott Weiland, and Zack de la Rocha. He eventually realized he couldn't sound like them and developed his own distinctive style. This unique vocal approach, combined with Ian's guitar playing, helped the band stand out from other Canadian bands of the era like Moist, Treble Charger, and The Tea Party. "I, the first five years of being in a band, you know, I was trying to sound like other people, you know, I was trying to sound like Eddie Vetter. I was trying to sound like Scott Watt. I'm trying to sound like Zack Delroch. You know, like, I'm trying to do that. And then I realized I can't do that, you know, so I just kind of ended up being me."
